name: Medical Device Innovation Corp.
old_description: In today’s competitive and entrepreneurial marketplace, the ability and vision to accelerate ideas from concept to market is instrumental in success and long-term profitability.  From validation and FDA regulatory filings to clinical trials, our integrated approach helps clients launch successful products and maximize profitability.
about:
Medical Device Innovation Corp. (MDIC) is based in Irvine, California, where it provides consulting and product development services for the medical device industry. The company focuses on accelerating ideas from concept to market through an integrated approach that spans validation, regulatory filings, and clinical trials.

MDIC offers a range of services including innovation management, ideation, intellectual property assessment, product development, design validation planning, regulatory filings (510(k), PMA, De Novo), clinical trial management, financial analysis, and supply chain setup. The firm also assists with prototyping, proof-of-concept validation, FDA design control and quality system regulation (QSR) documentation (DHF, DMR, DHR), commercial product design, manufacturing setup, and FDA validation.

The company serves medical device manufacturers, startups, and entrepreneurs seeking to bring new products to market. Its clients include organizations needing support with FDA clearance, clinical evidence generation, cost-of-goods reduction, and intellectual property strategy.

MDIC emphasizes an integrated, roadmap-driven approach that combines strategy, project management, and regulatory expertise to help clients maximize profitability and accelerate time to market.

name: Medical Products Laboratories
old_description: Medical Products Laboratories, Inc. is a full service contract manufacturer of human and veterinary pharmaceuticals,
about:
Medical Products Laboratories, Inc. (MPL) was founded in 1936 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company has operated as a contract manufacturer for nearly nine decades, though the INPUT does not specify its ownership structure or founders.

MPL provides full-service contract manufacturing and packaging for human and veterinary pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and nutritional supplements. Its capabilities span formulation development, production of liquid, semi-solid, and solid dosage forms, and a broad range of packaging formats including blisters, packets, pouches, bottles, jars, pumps, sprayers, tubes, syringes, and aerosols. The company maintains a diverse equipment fleet and adds new machinery regularly; its engineering team also fabricates custom tooling for unique packaging needs. Regulatory and compliance teams support clients from pilot scale through commercial production.

The company serves the pharmaceutical, veterinary, dietary supplement, and medical device industries, supplying both human and animal health markets. Customers range from drug and supplement brands to medical device firms seeking turnkey development and manufacturing.

MPL emphasizes its turnkey approach, covering the entire product life cycle from concept to end-stage production. It highlights exceptional value and flexibility derived from its extensive in-house equipment, continuous capital investment, custom tooling capability, and dedicated regulatory guidance.

name: Medicatech USA
old_description: Medicatech USA® is a leading manufacturer and distributor dedicated to providing high-quality radiographic solutions.
about:
Medicatech USA was founded in 2005 in Anaheim, California, as a manufacturer and distributor of radiographic solutions. The company began with a focus on digital radiography systems for both human medical and veterinary applications.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures a range of radiographic equipment including straight-arm and U-arm systems (MasteRad MX30, MX30C, MX40), mobile C-arms (Mini-X), flat-panel detectors (MasterX and EXPRIMER series), X-ray generators (NexGen 900 series), and portable veterinary units (ClearRay 1700, 2000, SIUI). It also develops the Voyance® image acquisition software and PACS platform, featuring the ClairVoyance™ deep-learning algorithm for bone suppression. Medicatech reports 42,785 powered facilities and 11,378 dealers served.

Medicatech serves human medical radiology, veterinary radiology, chiropractic imaging, and dental imaging markets. Its customers include hospitals, clinics, chiropractors, veterinarians, and a network of dealers across the United States.

The company emphasizes American-made manufacturing, rapid installation (under 15 minutes), US-based phone support, and custom engineering to modify products for specific clinical needs. Its stated mission is to deliver seamless, reliable radiology solutions that improve clinical efficiency and patient outcomes.

name: Medicreations
old_description: Uncompromising results. Empowering your growth — without sacrificing value.
about:
Medicreations is based in Las Vegas, Nevada. The company was founded by professionals with decades of combined experience in medical aesthetics and engineering, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. No ownership structure such as family, veteran, or woman-owned status is publicly stated. The founders recognized the challenges aesthetics professionals faced—lackluster service, unreliable warranties, and devices that did not deliver consistent ROI—and set out to build a different kind of device company.

Medicreations designs and manufactures a line of energy-based aesthetic devices at its FDA-audited facility in Las Vegas. The portfolio includes the MediSpa, a seven-modality facial platform; the Velo, an air-cooled CO2 laser for resurfacing and scarring; the MediDiode, a diode laser for hair removal across all skin types; the MediYag, a dual-wavelength Q-switched Nd:YAG system for pigmentation and tattoo removal; and the MediLight, an IPL platform with five wavelength filters. The company emphasizes USA-made quality, minimal consumables, and fast treatment times.

The devices are sold to medical aesthetics practices, medspas, dermatology clinics, and plastic surgery centers across the United States. Practitioners seeking ROI-driven technology and reliable support form the core customer base. The company highlights that its technologies power treatments for acne, anti-aging, skin tightening, pigmentation, tattoo removal, and hair removal.

Medicreations differentiates itself with a two-year warranty on every device—an uncommon promise in the industry—along with included training and ongoing support. All equipment is built in an ISO-certified, FDA-compliant facility, and the company stresses durable, USA-made construction, limited consumables, and minimal maintenance to lower operating costs for clinic owners.

name: Medway Plastics Corporation
old_description: We’re a company with Sustainable Plastic Injection Molding & Design since 1974,  working with the best machinery & tools. You can find us in Long Beach, California & Round Rock, Austin, Texas.
about:
Medway Plastics Corporation was founded in 1974 in Long Beach, California, and remains family-owned. The company operates a second facility in Pflugerville, Texas, near Austin. No founder names are disclosed in the source material.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding and design, offering single- and multi-cavity tooling for small, medium, and large parts. Its Long Beach plant runs 26 injection presses, 16 of which are 500 tons or larger, while the Pflugerville site operates four presses. Medway processes both commodity and engineering resins and recycles all plastic scrap back into production. A distinctive feature is its on-site electric co-generation system: three 375-kilowatt natural-gas generators with absorption chillers that supply electricity, recover heat for mold-cooling refrigeration, and provide whole-plant backup power.

Medway serves a broad range of industrial customers but does not name specific sectors in its public materials. The company also develops and sells proprietary products under its own brand.

Sustainability and energy independence are central to Medway's positioning. The co-generation system has operated for roughly 11 years, and the firm has added Thermal Control Solution radiant heating systems to its largest presses to further reduce energy consumption. The company emphasizes that its sustainable processes and material choices are driven by both environmental and cost-control objectives.

name: Melnick Metal Works Inc.
old_description: Since 1960, we’ve provided expert metal fabrication for residential, commercial, and industrial projects—built to last, made to fit.
about:
Melnick Metal Works Inc. has operated from Bristol, Connecticut since its founding in 1960. The third-generation, family-owned business began as a metal fabrication shop serving the local area and has continued under family stewardship for over six decades.

The company provides custom metal fabrication across a range of processes: cutting, bending, and shaping sheet metal for prototypes and production runs; building commercial and residential kitchen hoods in stainless steel; fabricating automotive brackets, panels, and structural parts for restoration and custom builds; producing railings for stairs, safety barriers, and decorative applications; constructing metal roofs and awnings for weather protection; manufacturing industrial components such as machine parts, enclosures, and structural elements; and creating architectural metalwork including decorative panels and structural components for buildings and public spaces. The shop's team of fabricators brings more than 100 years of combined experience to projects of varying scale.

Customers span residential, commercial, and industrial sectors. The company has supplied hoods to restaurants, railings to homes and businesses, automotive parts to classic-car restorers, and structural components to manufacturers and construction firms. A testimonial from New England Machine Tools references repeated intricate fabrications, while other clients note work on a Wagoneer rocker panel and custom hoods.

Melnick Metal Works emphasizes its experienced workforce, on-time delivery, and ability to handle jobs from small residential tasks to large industrial projects. The family-owned structure is cited as a foundation for its commitment to quality and long-term customer relationships.

Mercury Electronics, based in Seven Valleys, Pennsylvania, has been in continuous operation since 1946. The company provides electrical and electronic contract manufacturing services for commercial and military industries worldwide.

name: Mermar Electronics
old_description: ISO/AS9100 electronics manufacturer offering cable harness assembly plus PCB work
about:
Mermar Electronics is a contract electronics manufacturer based in Hesperia, California, founded in 1999. The company provides PCB fabrication, assembly, cable harness, box build, and electro-mechanical assembly services from a single facility in the High Desert region.

The company operates a state-of-the-art assembly plant capable of surface-mount, through-hole, and mixed-technology PCB assembly, including fine-pitch placement down to 01005/0201 components and BGA rework. It offers PCB fabrication, design, quick-turn prototyping as fast as 24 hours, and full box-build integration with testing, packaging, and labeling. Services cover prototype to high-volume production runs, with both consignment and turnkey material management options.

Mermar serves original equipment manufacturers in aerospace, medical, dental, therapeutic, telecommunications, industrial, renewable energy, kiosk, and guitar pedalboard markets. Its aerospace work is backed by AS9100 Rev D certification and ITAR registration, while medical assemblies follow ISO 9001:2015 and RoHS compliance.

The company emphasizes rapid turnaround, advertising same-day and next-day quick-turn assembly, 24-hour prototype builds, and a one-stop turnkey model that eliminates multi-vendor coordination. All products are built in the USA under a quality system that includes AOI, X-ray inspection, and adherence to IPC standards.

name: Metal Fab Engineering
old_description: Crafting Outstanding Solutions and Creating Remarkable Products for More than Five Decades
about:
Metal Fab Engineering operates from Winamac, Indiana, where it was founded in 1976 as a small fabrication shop by Paul Ezra and his wife Mary Lou. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the company has grown into a full-service metal fabrication partner for OEM manufacturers across the Midwest and beyond.

The shop runs four automated lasers capable of cutting carbon steel up to 1 inch, stainless steel up to 3/4 inch, and aluminum up to 1/2 inch. Its forming department includes over 20 press brakes, highlighted by a 225-ton press with an 8-foot bed and a 175-ton CNC unit with 12-foot beds. Robotic and manual welding cells handle welded subassemblies and final assemblies, while an in-house powder coating line provides durable finishes for low-to-mid volume runs. The company also offers value-add engineering, CAD-based design consulting, and a domestic-first procurement service. Annual output reaches hundreds of thousands of parts.

Metal Fab Engineering serves OEM manufacturers in a variety of industrial sectors, though specific verticals are not publicly listed. Its customer base includes companies that require precision laser-cut components, formed brackets, welded frames, and finished assemblies delivered through a single-source supply chain.

The company emphasizes problem-solving expertise backed by more than six granted patents and multiple pending applications. Its family-owned structure drives a culture of integrity and long-term partnership, recognized by a 2023 Safety Award of Honor from the Fabricators & Manufacturers Association. A domestic-first sourcing platform and in-house finishing further differentiate its offering.

Homeowners commission custom stair railings, gates, and interior metalwork; architects and contractors specify facades, sunshades, and structural elements; businesses order branded fixtures, signage, and commercial railings. The team collaborates directly with designers and builders to integrate metalwork into broader project plans.

Metalworking Group operates its Pippin Road facility in Cincinnati, Ohio, one of two plants the company runs in the city. The company produces sheet metal components, weldments, UL‑listed electrical enclosures, production stampings, stamping dies, fixtures, and CNC‑machined parts. Metalworking Group serves OEMs across the United States, Canada, and Western Europe. Its customer base spans defense and military, aerospace, medical device, fitness equipment, oil and gas, biogas reclaiming, border security, autonomous vehicle, industrial equipment, chemical dispensing, clean energy, material handling, and data‑center industries.

The firm emphasizes that ongoing investment in cutting‑edge equipment, top‑tier talent, and smarter workflows enables it to deliver precision‑built solutions and responsive support, aiming to function as an essential extension of its customers’ manufacturing teams. It holds UL Listing, ISO 9001, ITAR registration, and meets CMMC requirements for defense work.

about:
Meyer Wire & Cable Co. was founded in 1972 by Henry Meyer in Hamden, Connecticut. Originally located the company moved to its current facility in 1975.

The company designs and manufactures custom coil cords and cable assemblies, specializing in highly flexible, durable retractile cords rated for up to 20 million flex cycles. It produces both small custom batches and bulk cable runs (typically 1,000 feet), and offers a coiling service for customer-supplied cable with mandrel diameters from 0.125 to 2.25 inches and retracted lengths up to 96 inches. Value-added services include custom terminations—stripping, tinning, spade terminals, modular connectors, grommets, bands, and strain reliefs—as well as cable design support and in-process quality testing. Lead times for bulk cable are typically under three weeks, and quote requests are answered the same day.

Meyer Wire’s products serve a range of industries requiring flexible interconnect solutions, though the company does not publicly list specific sectors. Its cords are built to meet diverse application requirements, from easy-pull to rugged environments, and all products are RoHS and REACH compliant with UL-listed options available.

The firm emphasizes rapid response and small-run flexibility as key differentiators, rooted in a culture of “wire dedication” spanning three generations. Free coiling of customer-provided cable samples and free cord samples from stock further reduce development risk for clients.

Michaelson emphasizes its long‑standing reputation as New Jersey’s top auto recycler, attributing its longevity to unmatched customer service, a clean and well‑organized yard, and a commitment to keeping the family tradition alive. name: Michigan Milk Producers Association
old_description: Operated by MMPA subsidiary Middlebury Cheese Company LLC, the Middlebury plant specializes in producing barrel and delihorn cheeses sold to wholesale customers and under the
about:
Michigan Milk Producers Association (MMPA) is a dairy cooperative founded in 1916 and headquartered in Novi, Michigan. The member‑owned organization began as a collective of dairy farmers in the Great Lakes region and has grown to operate processing facilities across Michigan, Indiana, and Ohio.

The cooperative runs five dairy processing plants. Its largest facility in Ovid, Michigan, handles more than 5 million pounds of milk per day, producing butter, milk powder, condensed milk, cream, and ultrafiltered milk. A plant in Constantine, Michigan, processes nearly 3 million pounds daily into ultrafiltered milk, cream, and condensed skim milk, with an adjacent ethanol plant that converts dairy byproducts. In Remus, Michigan, a cottage cheese plant processes over 500,000 pounds daily. The Middlebury, Indiana plant, operated through the Middlebury Cheese Company subsidiary, focuses on barrel and delihorn cheeses sold wholesale and under the Heritage Ridge Creamery brand. The Canton, Ohio facility, home to the Superior Dairy and Creative Edge subsidiaries, produces fluid milk and ice cream for national distribution. A farm supply store in Mt. Pleasant serves members and the public.

MMPA sells dairy ingredients to food manufacturers that make salad dressing, infant formula, candy, ice cream, pudding, baked goods, cheese, and yogurt. Its retail brands supply ice cream and fluid milk directly to consumers. The cooperative also provides milk testing and farm supply services to its member farms across Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, and Wisconsin.

The association emphasizes quality and sustainability, noting its Safe Quality Foods certification, Green Agri‑Business designations for the Ovid and Constantine plants, and numerous World Dairy Expo championship awards. Members participate in the National Dairy F.A.R.M. program for animal care, and the cooperative maintains an FDA‑certified central laboratory for milk quality assurance.

about:
Micro-Tek Corporation operates from a 30,000-square-foot facility in Cinnaminson, New Jersey. The company was founded in 1965 by George Rogers as the Miniature Insulated Wire Company and incorporated under its current name in 1966. Now under third-generation family ownership, the business has grown from a small shop into a multi-generational manufacturer serving aerospace, medical, and industrial markets worldwide.

Micro-Tek specializes in custom drawing, flattening, stranding, insulating, cutting, and stripping of fine wire and cable down to .0009 inch (AWG #50). Its capabilities include PTFE fluoropolymer extrusion for coax cores, tubing, and cables; etching for bondability on PTFE, FEP, PFA, and ETFE; wire winding; and contract manufacturing. All processes—wire drawing, stranding, insulating, and tubing—are performed under one roof, supporting custom and short runs as well as high-volume production.

The company serves aerospace customers with micro-coaxial cable, shielded twisted pair cable, and high-performance coaxial core for avionics, satellite systems, and communication equipment. In the medical sector, it supplies PTFE coaxial core, flat wire, fluoropolymer tubing, and etched liners for surgical devices, diagnostic imaging, braiding, coiling, and sensors. Industrial clients use its custom wire and cable for automation systems and high-temperature manufacturing processes requiring chemical resistance and durability.

Micro-Tek emphasizes precision, holding tolerances as fine as ±0.0002 inch, and flexibility, offering small runs, large orders, and just-in-time or contract manufacturing. The company cites its decades of experience, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and long-term customer relationships as key differentiators.

The business is a second-generation, family-owned operation; Jan Davis’s father, Dave, began his career there in 1957 and owned the company for more than 25 years. Today, Chris and Jan Davis have led the firm for over 15 years, continuing a legacy of custom fabrication and machining that the company describes as spanning more than 50 years.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication and precision machining services. Its capabilities include custom fabrication, a full-service machine shop, precision tool and die work, prototype design and fabrication, shearing, cutting, bending, forming, punching, sawing, rolling, and welding. Midwest Sheet Metal serves customers across a variety of industries, with product lines that include racing components and custom semi-truck sunvisors. The machine shop’s expertise in automotive stampings, fuel-injection parts, and small electric motor components further reflects a client base in automotive racing, heavy trucking, and general industrial manufacturing.

The company emphasizes its combination of scale and personal attention: a broad inventory and full-service capacity paired with one-to-one customer service. Its differentiators include a multi-decade workforce, extensive press-brake tooling, and a reputation for craftsmanship delivered at competitive prices.

A rigorous vendor approval program requires third-party audits and annual re-qualification, while internal QA teams conduct facility visits. Competitive pricing, stable sourcing, and a comprehensive testing regimen — both in-house and via third-party labs — underpin its value proposition.

about:
Minnesota Valley Electric Cooperative (MVEC) is headquartered in Jordan, Minnesota. Founded on March 6, 1937, the cooperative was formed when three small electric organizations from Carver, Le Sueur, and Scott counties merged under President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal rural electrification program. The cooperative is owned by its member-owners and operates as a not-for-profit utility.

MVEC provides electric distribution service to more than 48,500 meters across a 968-square-mile territory spanning nine Minnesota counties: Blue Earth, Carver, Dakota, Hennepin, Le Sueur, Rice, Scott, Sibley, and Waseca. The cooperative purchases wholesale power from two generation providers and maintains its own distribution infrastructure, including regular maintenance and tree-trimming programs. MVEC’s stated mission is to be a energy partner with the privilege to serve, guided by values of safety, innovation, accountability, and cooperation. The cooperative emphasizes member ownership and local governance as its distinguishing features.

name: Modern Alpha Plastics Inc
old_description: Modern Alpha Plastics was formed in 1996 when two of Kansas City's most respected custom molders — Modern Plastics Molding (founded 1965) and Alpha Plastics — merged into a single shop with sixty combined years of precision injection experience.
about:
The company was formed in 1996 when Modern Plastics Molding (founded 1965 in Independence, Missouri) and Alpha Plastics (a Kansas City molder founded in the early 1960s) merged, combining sixty years of precision injection molding experience. Today the business is led by Anthony C. Gross, President and Chief Engineer, who oversees quoting and mold approvals directly.

The shop runs twenty-one injection molding presses ranging from 50 to 1,550 tons of clamp force, with shot capacities of 2 to 75 ounces and part weights from 5 grams to 10 pounds. Production volumes span 250 to over five million parts annually. In-house capabilities cover mold design, build, qualification, repair, and maintenance through vetted tooling partners, plus secondary operations including ultrasonic welding, CNC machining, sub-assembly, custom packaging, heat sealing, and pad printing. The company processes nine engineering-grade resin families along with commodity, glass-filled, mineral-filled, and impact-modified materials.

Modern Alpha serves aerospace and defense (ITAR-registered), medical device, drone and UAS, consumer, and industrial markets. Specific programs include structural drone brackets, legacy OEM re-engineering, metals-to-plastics conversions, thin-wall food-grade containers, and large industrial housings. Customers range from OEMs requiring close-tolerance components to firms needing turnkey design-to-distribution support.

The company emphasizes engineer-led, single-source responsibility — design, tooling, molding, assembly, and shipping under one purchase order. Statistical Process Control and Statistical Quality Control run on every press every shift, with material inspection at receiving, in-process evaluation, pre-shipping sign-off, and retained samples archived indefinitely. Long-tenured operators, some with thirty-year careers, provide tribal knowledge that the firm cites as a deliberate competitive advantage.

about:
Modern Process Equipment Corporation was founded in 1957 in Chicago, Illinois, where it maintains its worldwide headquarters. The company remains a family-owned business that has spent more than six decades designing, manufacturing, and supporting industrial process equipment for customers around the globe.

MPE builds precision particle-size-reduction equipment — including corrugated roller mills sold under the Gran-U-Lizer™ name, disc-style and roller-style coffee grinders (such as the compact SRM.MAX for espresso), and the Chain-Vey® tubular drag conveyor line for gentle, enclosed transport of bulk powders and fragile food products. The Process Systems Group integrates those machines into turnkey lines that handle classification, storage, pneumatic transport, mixing, coffee degassing, and clean-in-place automation. The company also operates grind and conveyor testing labs and runs an exchange program that restores worn rolls and heads to original condition.

The equipment serves coffee roasters (gourmet, industrial, capsule, turkish, and ultrafine), food processors (bakery, cereal, snack, peanut and tree nut, pet food), chemical and mineral producers, distilleries, breweries, and powder-and-bulk-solids handlers. Named references include Death Wish Coffee Company, Lawrence Foods, Westrock, Wicked Joe Coffee, Bird Foods, Pacifikava, a aviation supplier, a CPG brand, and a snack brand.

MPE states its purpose is to lead the invention, development, and manufacture of the industry's most advanced processing equipment and to translate that technology into customer value through professional solutions and unwavering support — including 24/7/365 virtual assistance, global on-site service on short notice, commissioning support, and operator training.

Mohawk Electrical Systems, Inc. is headquartered in Milford, Delaware. The company was founded in 1963 by Clarence and Stephen Welch. In 1988, Scott Welch joined the firm and became the third-generation owner in 2006, continuing family ownership.

The company operates as a basic-to-complex assembly integrator, combining precision manufacturing with quality components to produce custom assemblies. Core capabilities include bridgewire and ordnance products, electromechanical assemblies, cable and harness assemblies, and contract manufacturing. Processes encompass multi-conductor instrument cable, coaxial cable, specialty power cables, multi-point harnesses, and molded rubber components for turnkey assemblies.

Mohawk serves the defense, oil and gas, pyrotechnics, instrumentation, mining, and construction industries. Its products are used in military applications such as the M18A1 and M68 Claymore weapon systems, as well as in commercial explosive products for coal mining, dam construction, roads, railways, and other large projects. The company also supports oil and gas well perforating and pyrotechnic systems.

Mohawk emphasizes a reputation for superior quality and reliability of detonators in military applications. Its quality assurance program includes receiving inspection of all materials, infrared and video inspection technology, statistical process control during production, 100% line and final product inspection, and packing and shipping inspection. The firm states that this integrated approach delivers improved product quality, on-time delivery, and overall customer satisfaction.

The founders’ original goal was to keep Montana’s agricultural infrastructure running with reliable, local service. The Monterey Company operates from Bend, Oregon, where it has manufactured custom promotional products since 1989. The business began with a focus on challenge coins and patches for military and public‑safety organizations and has since expanded into a broad catalog of branded merchandise.

Minimum orders start at 25 pieces, with volume discounts on larger runs; the catalog lists thousands of SKUs.

Recent projects include challenge coins for the Indiana Army National Guard, custom belt buckles, embroidered patches for a firefighter apparel brand, and race medals for sporting events. The company also supplies nursing pins, letterman patches, and general promotional products such as apparel, magnets, and lanyards.

The Monterey Company emphasizes low minimums (25 pieces), free art proofs with unlimited revisions, a 2‑4 week standard turnaround, dedicated one‑on‑one account representatives, free domestic shipping, international shipping capability, pre‑production samples on request, and waived setup fees on exact reorders.

old_description: Solar Installation Throughout Midcoast Maine and the Islands of Penobscot Bay.
about:
Moody Mountain Solar operates from Searsmont, Maine, and was founded in the spring of 2020 by Cory Alexander. After 15 years in the boat-building industry and a lifetime of off-grid living at sea and on land, Alexander started the company to deliver a more personalized solar design and installation experience. The business remains owner-operated, with Alexander serving as the NABCEP-certified system designer and the single point of contact for every project.

The company installs rooftop arrays, ground-mount systems, and off-grid power solutions across Midcoast Maine and the islands of Penobscot Bay. Its rooftop work emphasizes roof integrity, drawing on building-trades experience to ensure watertight mounts on asphalt, metal, and EPDM surfaces. Ground-mount installations incorporate bifacial panels, while off-grid systems use modern lithium battery storage. Alexander is on site for the full installation, and the firm handles design, permitting, and commissioning in-house.

Customers include homeowners seeking grid-tied systems, seasonal camps replacing generators, and island properties requiring micro-grid independence. The service area covers coastal towns and remote islands where utility access is limited or unreliable.

Alexander founded Moody Mountain Solar to offer premium service at a reasonable cost while maintaining a neighborly, community-focused approach. The company differentiates itself by keeping the designer on the job site, providing a single contact from quote to commissioning, and applying marine-grade attention to detail to every roof penetration.

old_description: Our mission is to give landfill bound timber a second life by uncovering the hidden beauty within. With a focus on walnut, we are here to provide your first step to exploring the beauty and quality of locally-sourced lumber from Nashville and the surrounding areas.
about:
Nashville Wood operates from Nashville, Tennessee. The family-owned sawmill was first established in 2006 and re-established in 2023. The founders are not named, but the business began with a mission to rescue landfill-bound timber and give it a second life.

The company produces artistic lumber with a focus on walnut, all sourced locally from the Nashville area. Its process includes slabbing logs, air-drying the wood in flitches (keeping each log's boards together) rather than kiln-drying, and cutting every piece live edge so customers can decide final dimensions. The shop also offers custom milling and planing services. As a small family operation, it does not disclose facility size or headcount.

Primary customers are wood artists and furniture makers who value unique grain and color consistency across a project. The flitch-drying method allows clients to build entire pieces from matching lumber. The company also seeks partnerships with charitable organizations in need of lumber.

Nashville Wood differentiates itself by avoiding kiln drying to preserve natural wood colors, by keeping flitches intact for grain matching, and by selling exclusively live-edge slabs that let the end user control the final cut. The business was founded on the principle of diverting usable timber from landfills.

about:
New Jersey Textiles, Inc. traces its roots to 1945, when Israel Merdinger and his son Julius arrived in the United States from Poland and entered the rag trade in New York City. Starting with a hand truck, they collected wool clippings from garment factories in the Garment Center and transported them to what would become SoHo, eventually leasing warehouse space and purchasing a building to sort and bale the waste for export to overseas mills. The business later relocated to Clifton, New Jersey, where it operates today under the leadership of President David Merdinger.

The company functions as a wholesale fabric distributor, purchasing closeout and excess inventory from clothing manufacturers and jobbers throughout the New York–New Jersey metropolitan area. Its stock turns constantly and is sold by the yard, by the bolt, or by the pound. Current offerings include print chiffons, ITY prints, taffetas, and laces. In addition to fabric wholesaling, New Jersey Textiles continues to import and export wool clippings for reprocessing.

Customers span retail stores, apparel manufacturers, interior decorators, designers, and the home rug‑hooking trade across the United States. The firm positions itself as a low‑cost source for short‑run and specialty fabrics, with no minimum order mentioned in its public materials.

The operation began as a family effort to build a livelihood from post‑war textile waste, evolving over decades into a dual‑track business that both recycles wool by‑products and supplies discounted yard goods to a broad base of buyers.

about:
New Tech Plastics, LLC operates from Covington, Ohio. The company was founded in 1996 by John Weikert, Bill Weikert, Buck Siler, and Lew Coppock, who set out to build a first-class plastics business. In February 2025, the company was acquired by Flexible Packaging Partners (FPP), and is now owned by Jonah Sandler, Les Sandler, and Shawn Turner.

The company specializes in custom blown film extrusion, producing co-extruded films and poly bags for flexible packaging. Its facility spans four production plants on 20 acres, equipped with 15 extrusion lines and 20 material silos running 24/7. Capabilities include film thicknesses from 0.00035 to 0.010 mil, with additives such as antistatic, UV inhibitors, flame retardants, vapor corrosion inhibitors, antiskid agents, and color concentrates. A Channel Products line uses 100% recycled scrap for non-FDA applications like can liners and industrial sheeting.

New Tech Plastics serves agricultural, industrial packaging, consumer goods, and medical & pharmaceutical sectors, as well as manufacturing, food processing, logistics, and janitorial markets. Its films are used in automated form-fill-seal machines, shrink wrapping, and protective packaging.

Founded on a shared vision to lead the plastics industry, the company emphasizes zero-waste operations, domestic sourcing, and long-term customer relationships. Under FPP ownership, it continues to focus on innovation, fast turnaround, and nationwide delivery, positioning its thin-gauge films as a way to reduce material costs, shipping expenses, and environmental impact.

about:
Nichols Portland, Inc. (operating as Nichols Portland, LLC) is headquartered in Portland, Maine, with additional manufacturing facilities in Pennsylvania and Michigan. While no founding year or founder names are disclosed, the business has evolved into a multi-division manufacturer uniting sintered metals, pumps, precision valves, metal injection molding, and additive manufacturing under one brand.

The company produces gerotors, pumps, specialty valves, powder metal components, and metal injection molded parts, and offers metal additive manufacturing, custom machining, and product testing and analysis. Its capabilities span from prototyping through full-scale production, supported by engineering services that include design guidance, pump analysis, and application-specific manufacturing support. Facilities are described as state-of-the-art across three states, though headcount, floor space, and annual volumes are not published.

Nichols Portland serves OEMs in automotive, medical, industrial, off-highway, energy, construction, agriculture, marine, and heavy-truck markets. Nicolet Plastics operates from two Wisconsin facilities: a 41,000-square-foot plant in Mountain and a 31,000-square-foot plant in Jackson. The company was formed in 1986 when its founders, who began as a mold-making shop in the late 1980s, combined their tooling and molding operations under one name.

The molder runs 46 injection molding presses ranging from 30 to 610 tons across both sites, supported by advanced temperature controllers and real-time monitoring software. Core capabilities include custom plastic injection molding, specialized automated insert molding cells, tight-tolerance and micro molding, and additive manufacturing via Carbon 3D plastic printing and Mantle 3D metal printing. Post-molding services encompass CNC machining, ultrasonic and vibration welding, pad printing, over molding, heat staking, and both manual and automated assembly. The in-house tool room maintains customer molds and assists with design improvements, while engineering support covers design for manufacturability, prototype development, and metal-to-plastic conversion.

Nicolet serves equipment manufacturers in industrial, medical, marine, aerospace, consumer products, commercial goods, and sporting goods sectors. Its customer base includes well-known companies requiring complex parts molded from commodity and engineered resins.

The company highlights its cross-trained workforce and customer education program—recognized by Plastics News as a Best Place to Work for 2026 and a 2016 Insight Innovation Award winner for training. The tool-making heritage remains a differentiator, enabling mold maintenance and part-design optimization that reduce lead times and cost.

Norseman Designs West operates from Cody, Wyoming, where it was founded in 1971 by John Gallis. Before establishing the shop, Gallis spent 14 years as Bloomingdale's chief high-end cabinetmaker in New York. The business remains family-run, with his son Ian Gallis joining full-time 17 years ago after working alongside his father for two decades.

The company produces custom Molesworth-style furniture and luxury ranch pieces, a specialization it has held for the past 27 years. Each item is built in their Cody showroom and workshop using walnut, juniper, and distinctive burl wood for legs and drawer pulls. Details include leather upholstery, hand-painted panels, rawhide-sculpted accents, Chimayo woven textiles, and half-round pole construction. They accept designs ranging from formal drawings to napkin sketches.

Clients are primarily high-end residential owners and interior designers seeking authentic Western ranch aesthetics. The firm's work has been featured in Mountain Living, Cowgirl Magazine, Log Home Living, Big Sky Journal, and Cowboys & Indians. Projects span one-off commissions to full ranch furnishings, all tailored to individual rustic style preferences.

Gallis describes their philosophy simply: "We build furniture as if it were for ourselves. If it's not good enough for our house, it's not good enough for the client." That standard, combined with the ability to translate rough ideas into finished pieces, has sustained the shop for over five decades.

about:
Based in Dalton Gardens, Idaho, with a showroom in nearby Coeur d'Alene, North Idaho Log Furniture Company was founded in 1996 by Dan and Kelli Booterbaugh. The couple started the business as a small mountain workshop driven by a shared passion for woodworking and the outdoors.

The company handcrafts solid-wood log furniture for every room: beds, bunk beds, tables, chairs, dressers, cabinets, desks, nightstands, couches, mantels, and lamps. Using Lodgepole Pine, Ponderosa Pine, and Hickory harvested from North Idaho forests, each log is hand-selected, hand-peeled, sanded, and joined with traditional mortise-and-tenon construction. Finishes are eco-conscious stains and protective oils. The shop builds custom pieces to order and constructs custom pallets for each shipment, calculating freight individually rather than using a cart-based checkout.

The company serves homeowners, cabin builders, and interior designers across the United States. Customers range from individuals furnishing mountain cabins and lakeside retreats to design professionals specifying rustic pieces for residential projects.

The founders emphasize three principles: quality, integrity, and authenticity. They position their work as a continuation of Idaho craftsmanship, highlighting hand-built joinery, responsible sourcing, and a made-to-order model that avoids mass production. The goal is furniture that "lives with you" for generations.

old_description: Owned and operated by Peter Corr who began his 40 year custom home building career in 1969, and ending in 2008.
about:
Northeast Millwork Corporation operates from an 11,200-square-foot shop in Tiverton, Rhode Island. The company was founded in 1993 by Peter Corr, who had spent four decades in custom home building starting in 1969. Corr’s experience included constructing over 30 new homes, completing more than 100 renovations, and restoring six National Register properties. His work with antique wood began in 1981 through a partnership with Oliver Durfee’s Sawmill, where he specialized in sawing antique longleaf southern pine and reclaimed timber for post-and-beam homes.

The shop houses a 1949 Lane sawmill capable of cutting beams over 40 feet long and 36 inches wide, supplemented by a WoodMizer sawmill for beams up to 20 feet. Northeast Millwork produces antique heart pine flooring in vertical grain, plainsawn, and cabin grades, as well as antique American chestnut flooring. Custom millwork includes mantels, handrails, stair treads, newel posts, balusters, tables, doors, windows, dentils, brackets, countertops, casings, and moulding runs. The company also fabricates antique longleaf pine and American chestnut post-and-beam frames, and salvages materials from 1700s-era textile mills and houses, including granite, bluestone, brick, barn board, and original antique flooring. A current project involves restoring a 1985 Shannon 51-foot ketch.

The firm serves custom home builders, renovation contractors, and architects seeking historic wood elements for new construction, additions, and restoration projects. Commercial clients have included bars, restaurants, and metal building projects. The marine restoration portfolio covers historic J‑Boats such as Endeavor, Shamrock, Corrinett, and Cotton Blossom, along with Shannon yachts. Historic preservation work extends to six National Register homes.

Corr founded the millwork operation after recognizing that many of his building clients wanted the antique wood aesthetic incorporated into their projects, a demand that existing suppliers could not meet with authentic, large-dimension reclaimed material.

Northeast Solar is a residential energy services company based in Hatfield, Massachusetts, founded in 2015. The company serves homeowners across four counties in Western Massachusetts, offering integrated energy systems that combine solar generation, battery storage, heat-pump mini-splits, and electric-vehicle charging. The firm designs and installs complete home energy systems rather than selling standalone equipment. Its "Power Plan" assessment evaluates a home's current energy use, roof potential, and owner goals to specify a tailored mix of solar photovoltaics, Enphase microinverter-based storage, Mitsubishi Electric mini-splits, and EV chargers. All installation work is performed by Northeast Solar's own licensed employees; the company does not use subcontractors. Since inception it has completed more than 2,000 installations.

The customer base consists exclusively of residential property owners in Western Massachusetts seeking to replace variable utility bills with fixed-cost energy, improve resilience during grid outages, and reduce heating and cooling expenses. Typical projects include solar leases with zero down payment and a 25-year fixed rate, mini-split retrofits that qualify for Mass Save rebates up to $8,500, and battery systems that provide backup power.

Northeast Solar differentiates itself by maintaining a single, directly employed crew across all trades, a 10-year workmanship warranty, and certifications including A+ Better Business Bureau rating (since 2015), Enphase Gold Installer status, Mitsubishi Diamond Installer status, and Mass Save Certified Heat Pump Installer designation. The company emphasizes long-term local support over rapid growth.

about:
Northern Wire operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Merrill, Wisconsin. Established in 1970, the company has grown into one of the country's largest custom wire-forming operations and now operates as part of the MW Components family, the largest single-source supplier of specialty fasteners in the nation.

The company manufactures complex wire forms, specialty bends, and welded products with wire processing capabilities extending up to 12 feet. Its shop runs 25 presses ranging from 10 to 600 tons for flattening, punching, and staking, plus resistance and wire-feed welding. Northern Wire combines automated CNC wire bending with manual forming to handle geometries that automation alone cannot achieve, and it performs a full suite of secondary operations in house — including chamfering, coining, drilling, extruding, grooving, knurling, machining, piercing, tapping, and threading — alongside standalone zinc plating and powder coating services.

Northern Wire serves original equipment manufacturers and blue-chip wholesalers and distributors across aerospace, agriculture, appliances, construction, consumer goods, energy, industrial, lawn and garden, medical, power equipment, and recreation markets. Its blended sourcing model pairs domestic quality control with licensed product manufacturing and design consultation to mitigate supply-chain disruptions.

The company emphasizes engineering excellence and quality at all levels, holding ISO 9001:2015 certification and QSLM Class 2 compliance with tools calibrated and traceable to NIST. In-house secondary services and a barcode-driven distribution system are cited as key factors in reducing lead times for time-sensitive deliveries.

about:
Northwind Solar was established in 2007 in Amherst, Wisconsin. In 2013 the company transitioned to a worker‑owned cooperative, meaning the technicians and designers who install each system are also the owners of the business. The cooperative model was adopted to align long‑term company health with customer success.

The firm provides turnkey solar photovoltaic and battery storage solutions for residential, commercial, agricultural, nonprofit, and municipal customers across 19 counties in Central Wisconsin. Its in‑house team handles site evaluation, shade analysis, system design, financial modeling, incentive and grant applications (including Focus on Energy and USDA REAP), utility interconnection, permitting, installation, commissioning, and ongoing service. Installations are performed by NABCEP‑credentialed designers and licensed electricians, and the company has deployed megawatts of distributed solar generation since its founding.

Customers range from homeowners and family farms to businesses, schools, faith communities, and local government facilities in communities such as Wausau, Marshfield, Stevens Point, Appleton, and Oshkosh. Projects include rooftop and ground‑mount arrays, solar‑plus‑storage systems, EV charging infrastructure, and energy monitoring platforms.

Northwind Solar differentiates itself through its worker‑owned structure, which eliminates commissioned sales and ensures the same personnel support a system years after installation. The company backs its work with a 10‑year workmanship warranty, uses components from brands such as Tesla, Qcells, IronRidge, Enphase, and Franklin Whole Home, and relies heavily on referrals and repeat business.

about:
NovelCath, a Cirtec Medical company, operates from Minneapolis, Minnesota. The brand was strengthened in July 2021 when Cirtec acquired Cardea Catheter Innovations, a vertically integrated manufacturer of minimally invasive catheter devices based in San Jose, California, and folded its operations into the NovelCath name. The business focuses on the design, development, and manufacture of highly engineered catheter delivery systems for interventional medicine.

The company runs a 20,000-square-foot vertically integrated facility that houses clean-room assembly, dedicated prototyping lines, catheter assembly, extrusion, braiding, coiling, and multiple reflow technologies. Recent expansion added Nitinol processing capabilities including laser cutting, heat setting, electropolishing, EDM, 5-axis machining, and grinding. The engineering team supports customers from early-stage concept verification through animal studies and into production, emphasizing long-term manufacturability.

NovelCath serves medical-device OEMs and start-ups in three clinical areas: structural heart, electrophysiology, and neurovascular. Its product portfolio includes EP mapping and ablation catheters, structural heart valve delivery and repair systems, steerable multi-directional catheters, and neuro microcatheters. The company also produces braided and coiled reinforced sheaths, offering a range of braid patterns, wire types, and durometer configurations tailored to torque, flexibility, and tip-articulation requirements.

NovelCath differentiates itself through its vertically integrated Nitinol tubing and processing services, quick-turn prototyping, and a leadership team with over 70 years of combined experience solving complex steerable and multi-directional catheter shaft designs. As a division of Cirtec Medical, it leverages broader organizational resources while maintaining a focused, responsive approach to catheter development.

old_description: Get 2-day delivery throughout the US for less than the typical price of ground shipping.
about:
OSH Cut operates from Spanish Fork, Utah, as an on-demand metal fabrication shop. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, nor are its founders named in available sources.

The shop runs a digital-first production line centered on laser cutting, tube laser cutting, bending, tapping, and flat finishing. Cutting is performed on 10 kW Trumpf 3030 fiber lasers, a 7 kW Trumpf 7000 tube laser, and an 8 kW Mazak Optiplex, all driven by in-house software that ties the online quoting and DFM engine directly to the machine controllers. Deburring uses a 120-grit wide-belt sander and graining a 240-grit belt. Bending capacity reaches 3/4 inch thickness in steel, stainless, aluminum, and copper; tapping covers 6-32 through 1 1/2-6 and M3 through M36. Powder coating is also offered. Standard cutting tolerance is ±0.005 inch.

Customers span aerospace, medical devices, astronomy, and the FIRST Robotics FRC community, alongside general prototyping and low-volume production buyers. The platform accepts a wide range of CAD files—including STEP, SLDPRT, DXF, and SVG—and ships to all 50 states via parcel or LTL freight.

OSH Cut emphasizes its instant quoting app with real-time DFM feedback and forming simulation, which lets users upload complex geometries that other vendors reject. The company advertises two-day delivery across the United States and positions its software-driven workflow as the primary differentiator.

It also manufactures its own HCX helical cutterheads and inserts, a product line developed over more than 20 years of cutterhead engineering.

Oliver serves high-end hobbyists and small commercial woodworking operations through its Heritage Collection of smaller-capacity tools, while its broader equipment lineup targets professional woodworking shops and industrial users.

The company’s early innovations — such as the 1908 round cutterhead that replaced hazardous square cutterheads and an early dado blade patent still in use — established a reputation for safety and durability that continues to inform its current helical cutterhead designs.

about:
On The Spot Assembly operates from Granger, Texas, in the Central Texas corridor near Austin's Silicon Hills. The company was founded in 2011 by Ernest G., who launched the business after more than 15 years in the electronics industry, including roles at multiple startups focused on RF and analog applications where he handled IC layout and full circuit-board assembly.

The shop specializes in quick-turnaround micro-electronic assembly for prototype and mid-volume runs with no minimum order quantity. Its privately owned facility houses a precision placement machine (PPM) for SMT placement, magnification workstations for hand assembly, custom fine-pitch solder stations, a framed stainless-steel stencil system accepting sheets up to 23 by 23 inches, and an ultrasonic cleaner using 99.9% isopropyl alcohol or de-ionized water. Processes cover surface-mount and through-hole placement, single- and double-sided boards, fine-pitch components down to 0201 and 0.35 mm QFN/DFN packages, BGA, TQFP, PLCC, and QFN assembly, as well as prototype rework including trace repair, component stacking, and fine-wire modifications.

Customers include engineering teams at startups and established firms developing RF, analog, and mixed-signal hardware in the Central Texas region. The company supports the full prototype iteration cycle, offering phased batch deliveries, on-site rework assistance, and courier service for local clients.

The founder established OTSA to simplify and accelerate the PCB assembly process, reducing product development time for innovators. The operation emphasizes honest communication, diligent workmanship, and a well-defined IPC Class 2–based process that can be customized per project, with a guarantee to resolve any issues that arise.

about:
Ozark Solar is based in Bella Vista, Arkansas. Founded in 2007 by Josh Whittle, who serves as owner, the company began with a focus on bringing energy independence to a four-state region covering Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, and Kansas.

The firm provides solar installation and roofing services. Its offerings include grid-tied solar systems, hybrid off-grid/grid-tied systems, commercial solar installations, residential roofing repair and replacement, off-grid solar systems using Fortress Power equipment, whole-home Generac generator installations, and solar panel detachment and reset services. The company reports that its installations have generated over 1.7 gigawatts of solar energy to date.

Ozark Solar serves residential and commercial customers across its service area. Residential clients include homeowners seeking grid-tied or off-grid power, as well as remote cabins, farms, and homesteads. Commercial clients range from small businesses to larger facilities requiring roofing and solar solutions.

The company emphasizes integrity and transparency, stating it is fully bonded and offers financing options with $0 down for qualified applicants. It also assists customers in claiming the 30% federal investment tax credit. A noted operational differentiator is a 7- to 14-day turnaround for solar panel detachment and reset work.

name: P D & E Electronics LLC
about:
PD&E Electronics operates from North Hampton, New Hampshire, where it was founded in 1967 as a semiconductor company serving a dozen local customers in the Boston area. The business began by building custom assemblies for semiconductor manufacturers and expanded through the acquisition of three product lines: ITT Selenium Division, Curtis-Wright Thermal Relays, and the North Hills RF Coil Line.

Today the company functions as a full-service custom electronics provider with design, manufacturing, and testing capabilities. Its product portfolio spans discrete rectifiers, rectifier modules, high-voltage and high-power rectifiers, printed circuit board assemblies (single- or multi-layer, through-hole or surface-mount), voltage regulators, power supplies (AC-DC, DC-AC, DC-DC converters and custom designs), and a range of custom assemblies including circuit cards, panels, filters, encapsulated servo amplifiers and indicator display lights. The firm also produces relays, flashers and sensors such as solid-state time delays, voltage monitors and ground-fault detectors. It reports manufacturing tens of thousands of distinct component types.

Customers include semiconductor companies, industrial OEMs and U.S. defense agencies. PD&E has acted as a second source for devices originally supplied by brands such as HV Component Associates, ITT Semiconductor, Microsemi/Unitrode, Semtech, Sensitron and others, offering improved delivery and pricing while meeting or exceeding original specifications.

The company emphasizes quality through in-process inspection, screening and final testing, citing an average quality rating of approximately 98 percent over two decades. It differentiates itself with engineering oversight of hand-built assemblies, custom design assistance from concept to completion, and a support staff that includes engineers, quality managers and production specialists.
